architecture_summary: Guard v2 foundation is a side-by-side strangler layer: bounded contracts and codecs, immutable domain state, CAS-oriented application use cases, and safe console tests. No Windows service, named-pipe host, cloud endpoint, browser extension, privileged adapter, or live enforcement action exists in this increment.

infrastructure.secret_management: No production secrets in scope; future service state and private keys remain behind unimplemented ports.

stride_summary.spoofing: Canonical parent trust anchors and exact pending-request validation are modeled; real client-token and ECDSA verification remain service work.
stride_summary.tampering: Signed canonical commands, CAS state transitions, strict codecs, and reducer invariants fail closed.
stride_summary.repudiation: Sequence and command-id state is durable by contract; production audit journal remains service work.
stride_summary.information_disclosure: Setup stores a secret hash and public trust anchor only; production encrypted storage remains service work.
stride_summary.denial_of_service: IPC frames, read time, replay history, payload size, and concurrent handler count are bounded by contract.
stride_summary.elevation_of_privilege: Child/admin/proxy verb allowlists exist; real named-pipe SID and DACL enforcement remains service work.

notes: The prior report was comprehensive; this report is limited to the new Guard v2 foundation scope, so persistent legacy findings were not re-audited here.
.gstack is not ignored by the repository and remains deliberately unstaged with other user-owned review artifacts.
No Guard executable, installer, Cleaner, AppLocker, firewall, hosts, registry, scheduled-task, service, or other live system action was run.
